title: What Are Futures & Options (F&O) and Why Are They Making News?
description: Futures & Options (F&O) are financial contracts whose value comes from an "underlying asset" like a stock or a market index. They let you bet on future price .

faq.a: It's the security (like a specific stock or a market index) on which the F&O contract is based. The value of the F&O contract changes as the price of this underlying asset changes.

faq.q: What is a "strike price" in Options?
faq.a: The strike price is the predetermined price at which the buyer of an Options contract can buy (for a Call Option) or sell (for a Put Option) the underlying asset.
Margin is the initial amount of money you need to deposit with your broker as a security deposit to enter into an F&O contract. It's a fraction of the total value of the contract.

faq.q: Can I lose more money than I initially invested in F&O?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. Especially when selling (writing) Options or trading Futures, your losses can exceed your initial margin amount if the market moves significantly against your position.

faq.q: Who regulates F&O trading in India?
faq.a: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the primary regulator for the securities market, including F&O trading, in India.
